requestedActions.title: List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination

prohibitions: Never create, edit or delete repositories
guide.summary: Forgejo provides an instance-wide OAuth2 provider using Authorization Code with PKCE, for confidential or public clients. Each instance needs an OAuth application registered in user settings, supplying client ID, secret, and redirect URI. Access tokens are Bearer tokens. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so tokens act fully as the user and cannot be restricted to read-only at the provider. Visible repositories can be listed via the search endpoint (private defaults to true) with page and limit. The app must enforce read-only behavior. Registration, consent, and token exchange are first-test setup requirements, not resource actions.

findings.title: Forgejo instance OAuth2 Authorization Code flow with PKCE is documented
findings.detail: Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code Grant with PKCE, and the documented endpoints are authorization, access token, and userinfo on the customer's instance base URL.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using the instance base URL as input.

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)
Authorization Endpoint /login/oauth/authorize Access Token Endpoint /login/oauth/access_token

findings.title: OAuth2 tokens have no scope restriction and may carry administrative rights
findings.detail: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented, and the token can execute any action on behalf of the user, not only Git actions. Third-party applications that obtain a token through an OAuth application have administrative rights. Read-only behavior therefore depends on the app itself, not on a token boundary.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to every OAuth connection for listing repositories, including customer instances.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.
Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.

findings.title: Register an OAuth application on each customer instance before the first test
findings.detail: Registration is documented under user settings for the application. Client credentials and the redirect URI are required. Choose confidential or public client type; public clients must be registered as public. Loopback redirect URIs are allowed for public clients.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer's own Forgejo instance must have a registered OAuth application before the connection can be tested.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: Connected person must have access to the repositories to be listed
findings.detail: Tokens are sent as Bearer headers to the API and act for the authorizing user. The connected person's existing account access determines which repositories are visible. Confirm representative access as a user prerequisite, since no additional OAuth scope is documented for that access.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to each customer account connecting to list visible repositories.

steps.title: Register an OAuth application on the customer's Forgejo instance
steps.detail: Create an OAuth2 application in the customer's own Forgejo user settings (/user/settings/applications), choosing confidential or public client type and a redirect URI. Record the client ID and client secret. Use <INSTANCE_BASE_URL> as the customer-supplied HTTPS base URL.
steps.doneWhen: The application exists on the customer instance and its client ID, secret and redirect URI are recorded for the test.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer-supplied HTTPS base URL of their Forgejo instance
CLIENT_ID: issued when the OAuth application is registered
CLIENT_SECRET: issued at registration; shown only once
REDIRECT_URI: must match the redirect used in the authorization request

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: After the customer consents at /login/oauth/authorize, POST the returned code to the documented token endpoint with client credentials, grant_type authorization_code and the matching redirect_uri. This step is documented but not executed by the agent.
steps.doneWhen: The token endpoint returns an access_token and token_type bearer for the connected account.

steps.title: List the first page of visible repositories
steps.detail: Call the repository search endpoint with private defaults to true so accessible private repositories are included. Use a documented page and limit. Read-only.
steps.doneWhen: The response returns a JSON array of repositories with names, and the Link and x-total-count headers are captured for pagination. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: ## GET /api/v1/repos/search | Search for repositories
Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: bearer token returned by the token exchange
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Request following repository pages until the collection ends
steps.detail: Use the documented next link from the Link header of the prior response, resolving any relative href against the same HTTPS instance host, and repeat with returned state until no next link remains. Continuation of the first listing request. Resolve the next link from the prior response and repeat until the documented end condition (no rel=next link).
steps.doneWhen: Every page is retrieved until the response no longer includes a rel=next link, and the total count matches the number of names collected. No further rel=next link is returned and all pages are collected. Boundary check: inspect the actual grant against the documented access above; confirm the outgoing request log contains only the requested operations and no prohibited actions.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is

The default and maximum values for the page parameter can be obtained from the https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/settings/api endpoint.
